newsitem.title: FRANCE: Lyon airport sees Jan-June 13.8 pct cargo growth.
newsitem.headline: Lyon airport sees Jan-June 13.8 pct cargo growth.

text.p: Lyon-Satolas airport said it recorded double-digit growth in flown airfreight in the first six months of 1997 compared to the first half of last year.
"January-June flown airfreight was up 13.8 percent to 11,913 tonnes, of which 47.3 percent was transported on all-cargo flights," a freight traffic spokesman for the airport authority told Reuters.
January-June 1997 full-freighter flights at Lyon-Satolas totalled 3,520, up 41.3 percent on the same period in 1996, airport authority figures showed.
He said the growth in traffic was largely due to increasing volumes of express traffic, which represented just under 50 percent of global airfreight handled at Lyon-Satolas.
Another factor had been the operation in recent months by Air Algerie of ad-hoc, full-freighter Lockheed Hercules L382G flights, notably carrying shipments of chicks to Algeria, the spokesman added.

"Air Algerie is planning more flights for this type of freight in the months to come and there is also a project to create a scheduled all-cargo service, although there are no specific details at this stage," the spokesman said.
